conversation.purpose: Track the child protective services interview against its investigative goals. Capture the child's account of the reported incident, assess immediate safety risks, identify inconsistencies between participant accounts, and flag topics that remain unaddressed or need clarification. Suggest follow-up questions to help the CPS worker assess the child's safety and the caregiver's protective capacity.
pay_attention_to: Child's direct disclosure of abuse, fear, or unsafe conditions
Inconsistencies between the child's, parent's, and caregiver's accounts
Physical injury details, severity, and whether medical care was sought
Child's emotional state, distress signals, and willingness to speak
Parent or guardian's protective response and believability
Identification of all household members and caregivers present

topics_to_cover.label: Consent & Interview Setup
criteria: Recording consent obtained from all participants before the interview began
Each participant introduced themselves or was identified by name or role
Child's age and current school grade confirmed
Agency's purpose for the visit explained to the family

topics_to_cover.label: Caregiver Identification
criteria: Caregiver's full name provided
Caregiver's relationship to the child confirmed
Whether caregiver lives in the home established
Caregiver's typical presence and role during the day noted

topics_to_cover.label: Injury Assessment
criteria: Type and location of the injury documented
Timeline of when the injury was first noticed established
Parent or guardian's explanation for the injury obtained
Medical examination sought and outcome documented
Injury formally recorded or referred for medical review

topics_to_cover.label: Child Safety & Fear Assessment
criteria: Child asked directly about their safety or comfort at home
Child identified a specific person they feel unsafe with
Child provided specific examples of threatening or harmful behavior
Child's disclosure explored with follow-up questions until fully understood
Child's overall emotional state and wellbeing assessed

topics_to_cover.label: Prior History & Pattern of Abuse
criteria: Previous incidents of injury or abuse involving the child asked about
Any prior CPS involvement or reports discussed
Pattern of the caregiver's behavior over time explored
Other adults or witnesses to past incidents identified

topics_to_cover.label: Household & Other Children
criteria: All adults living in the household identified
Other children in the home identified by name and age
Sleeping and care arrangements for the child documented
Any other individuals who regularly have access to the child noted

topics_to_cover.label: Safety Planning & Next Steps
criteria: Immediate safety plan for the child discussed with the parent
Specific actions the parent agreed to in order to protect the child
Whether emergency removal or alternative placement was considered
Follow-up visit or interview date and time agreed upon

fields.AllegedIncident: Hit child in eye with a thrown cup

crm_content.description: Child came to school with a black eye. Child told school staff that a man named Dave, who cares for her while mom works, threw a cup at her and hit her eye. Child said Dave gets angry and hits her with objects regularly.

sections.label: Record Check
sections.instruction: Compare the conversation so far against the CRM record provided. For each field and claim in the record, note whether it was confirmed, contradicted, or not mentioned during the conversation. Clearly state what the record says and what the conversation revealed.

sections.label: Case Narrative Summary
sections.instruction: Write a brief factual narrative of the conversation — who was present, what concern was reported, what key information was established, and how the interview ended. Write it as a case note an investigator would file.

sections.label: Red Flags & Risk Indicators
sections.instruction: List specific statements, behaviors, or observations from the conversation that indicate potential risk to the child's safety. For each item, quote or closely paraphrase what was said and explain why it is a concern.

sections.label: Conflicting Accounts
sections.instruction: Identify specific points in the conversation where participant accounts differ or contradict each other. For each conflict, state what each participant said and what remains unresolved.

sections.label: Child's Direct Statements
sections.instruction: List the most significant things the child said during the conversation, quoted or closely paraphrased. Focus on statements about safety, fear, injury, or the people in her life. These are the child's own words and should be preserved accurately.

sections.label: Investigator's Next Steps
sections.instruction: Based on the conversation, list the specific follow-up actions the investigator should take before closing this visit. Be concrete — name who to contact, what to ask, and what to document. Do not repeat what was already covered in the interview.
